description: The 34 compared solutions of poverty, each a part of the solution poverty research. Chain per solution: the share of the loss of poverty that the solution avoids if it is fully in place (reduction potential) times the probability that it is fully in place (fulfillment probability) gives the loss reduction; the loss reduction times the welfare loss share of poverty, the world htp and the poverty gain factor gives the potential gain in billion htp; the cost to set up the solution worldwide in billion USD times the person years per billion USD gives the initial effort in person years. Every reduction potential, probability and cost is assumed and has its own 80 percent probability range. The inputs of the welfare loss share of poverty are repeated from problem_poverty.json, so that the gain can be calculated within this file. The table of the poverty solutions has its own columns, the solution, the loss reduction in percent, the potential gain in htp and the initial effort in person years, sorted by the biggest potential gain on top.

formulas.name: probability range low
formulas.description: the lower bound of the probability range of an estimate, the estimate multiplied by its low range factor; the centre is the stated target value and each bound is calculated on its own, so that a range can be asymmetric

formulas.name: probability range high
formulas.description: the upper bound of the probability range of an estimate, the estimate multiplied by its high range factor; the centre is the stated target value and each bound is calculated on its own, so that a range can be asymmetric

formulas.name: long run damage share of the GDP
formulas.description: the share of the world GDP that a problem costs at the end of its development, the share it costs today multiplied by the factor by which the damage still grows; the share is stated negative, because it is a loss

formulas.name: welfare damage share
formulas.description: the share of the global happy time points that a problem costs, the share of the GDP it costs multiplied by the factor by which the welfare damage exceeds the money damage, because htp counts the healthy life years that the GDP does not (concept paper introduction)

formulas.name: avoided welfare loss with a gain factor
formulas.description: the happy time points that a solution saves, like the avoided welfare loss, but multiplied by a factor of the problem, because the shared world htp is tuned to one problem and does not fit the others until the horizon of the ranking is stated; the result is stated positive, because it is a gain

formulas.name: loss reduction of a solution part
formulas.description: the share of the potential loss of a problem that one part of its solution avoids, the share of the loss it avoids if it is fully in place multiplied by the probability that it is fully in place; the same measure as the loss reduction of the whole solution in the start page ranking

formulas.name: initial effort of a solution part
formulas.description: the person years needed to set up one part of a solution, its cost in billion USD multiplied by the person years per billion USD
formulas.expression: "initial effort","person year" = "initial effort","billion","USD" * "person year per billion USD","factor"

the cost to set up the solution worldwide: the cost of the assets and the coaching

the probability that the solution is fully in place: less likely, because most of the extreme poor work outside the tax system; about 2 billion workers or 61 percent of the employed worldwide work informally, and more than 85 percent in Africa (ILO 2018)
the cost to set up the solution worldwide: the cost of the credits

the probability that the solution is fully in place: even odds, because universal benefits are rare in poor countries; 1.77 billion children have no child or family cash benefit (ILO and UNICEF 2023)
the cost to set up the solution worldwide: the cost of the payments

the probability that the solution is fully in place: unlikely, because the sum is beyond the budget of poor countries

the share of the loss of poverty that the solution avoids if it is fully in place: a medium-small share, because the old poor are a smaller group

the probability that the solution is fully in place: likely, because social pensions spread in many countries; 77.5 percent of the people above retirement age already get some old-age pension (ILO 2021)
the cost to set up the solution worldwide: the cost of the pensions

the probability that the solution is fully in place: even odds, because coverage grows but slowly
the cost to set up the solution worldwide: the cost of the subsidised premiums

the share of the loss of poverty that the solution avoids if it is fully in place: a medium-small share, because a road raises the price a farmer gets; in Bangladesh paved rural roads reduced poverty through higher farm output, higher wages, lower transport costs and higher prices for the crops, with the largest gains for the poor (Khandker et al. 2009)
the probability that the solution is fully in place: likely, because roads are popular and funded
the cost to set up the solution worldwide: the cost of the roads
